svg.title: Language families and the scripts that write them
svg.desc: 4517 languages with a script on record, in 198 families and isolates on the left, joined by bands to the 115 scripts they are mainly written in on the right, ordered as the descent tree. Band thickness is the number of languages.
svg.text: LANGUAGE FAMILIES AND THE SCRIPTS THAT WRITE THEM
4,517 languages with a script on record, each counted once, under its main script. The other 4,070 have none on record and are not drawn.

svg.text: Band colour is the script's great lineage (key above). A language with several scripts is counted once, under its main script.
Script and family do not line up: Latin alone writes 3,610 of these languages, from families on every continent, while most other scripts serve one family.

40 families and isolates are drawn by name; the other 156 are pooled, as are the 85 scripts after the first 30. Glottolog's filing categories (Bookkeeping, Unclassifiable and the rest) are pooled as one.
Sources: Glottolog 5 CLDF (CC-BY-4.0); Wikidata P282, Unicode CLDR and SIL langtags for scripts. Built by render_families.py from out/dataset.json.
